$comment: What a bus log shows of a payload, as every bus log must show it. With SEMIONT_BUS_LOG set, a Semiont SDK or service writes one line for each frame it sends or receives, and the last thing on a line is the frame's payload. No line holds a credential. THE RULE reads a name and no channel: the value of a member whose whole name is one of `names`, letter for letter and in the same case, is shown as the text `[withheld]`, wherever in a payload the member is (in the payload itself, in an object within it at any depth, in an object inside an array) and whatever its value is (text, a number, null, an object, an array: the whole value is replaced, and nothing within it is read). THE NAMES are the ones a credential goes by. The registry's payloads declare one credential, the token a resource is cloned by, and name it `token` (`yield:clone-resource-requested` and `yield:clone-create`, which a client sends, and the `response` of `yield:clone-token-generated`, which it receives). But some payloads take any member (an agent's `parameters`, a job's `params` and its `result`, a graph's `metadata`, what a description of a resource or of a representation adds), and a credential put in one is withheld under the name it has elsewhere: `cloneToken`, an upload's name for the token a resource is cloned by; `accessToken` and `refreshToken`, a sign-in's two tokens, and `access_token` and `refresh_token`, as an issuer names them; `apiKey`, an inference provider's key as a knowledge base's configuration names it, and `api_key`, as a Python program does; `clientSecret` and `client_secret`, a service's secret at its issuer, as a program and as the grant that spends it name it; `secret` and `password`; and the header a credential is sent under, which is `authorization` and `Authorization` (two spellings of one header) and, for a provider's key, `x-api-key` and `x-goog-api-key`. A name that only contains one of them is another name, and is shown: a count of a model's tokens (`maxTokens`), a plural (`tokens`), another case (`Token`), the member that names the environment variable a credential is read from (`apiKeyEnv`, `passwordEnv`), an endpoint (`tokenEndpoint`). Everything else is shown as it is: every other member, an array's items in their order, a value that happens to be one of the names. A frame's payload is an object, and so is every case's. A log that can be given a payload that is not one reads an array by the same rule and shows anything else as it is, and holds that in its own tests. A case is a `payload` and what is `shown` of it. How a log writes what it shows (as JSON, as a console's rendering of an object) is its own, so a runner compares values and never text. Every name has a case of its own, and no case withholds under a name that is not listed. A case that is a channel's own payload names the `channel`, and its `payload` is one the registry's schema for that channel admits. Every bus log runs it, in whatever language it is written. A runner that has the registry's payload types holds each case that names a channel to that channel's payload type, the cases to `names`, and `names` to the members the registry's payloads declare. Add a name and its case here before changing an implementation.

cases.why: yield:clone-resource-requested, as a client sends it: the request is its token
yield:clone-create, as the gateway has it: the token is withheld, and what it rides with is shown, the gateway's stamp included
yield:clone-token-generated, as a client receives it: the token is a member of the reply's response
a token deep in a payload is withheld, and the members beside it at each depth are shown
a token in an object inside an array is withheld, in each object that has one, and the array keeps its order
an array inside an array is read too
a token that is a number is withheld, and is shown as the same text
a token that is null is withheld: the name decides, not the value
a token that is true or false is withheld
a token that is the empty text is withheld
a token that is an object is withheld whole: nothing within it is read or shown
a token that is an array is withheld whole
a name that only contains the word is another name, and is shown: the counts of a model's tokens the protocol carries, a plural, another case
a value that is the word, or the text a token is shown as, is no member of the name
a payload with no token is shown as it is: text of any script, numbers, null, and what is empty
the empty payload is shown as it is
cloneToken, which is what an upload names the token a resource is cloned by
accessToken, a sign-in's access token as a program's record of it names it
access_token, the same as an issuer's reply names it: what says its kind and how long it lasts is shown
refreshToken, a sign-in's refresh token as the sign-in store names it
refresh_token, the same as an issuer and a refresh grant name it: the grant's kind, whose value is the name, is shown
apiKey, an inference provider's key as a knowledge base's configuration names it, among an agent's parameters
api_key, the same as a Python program names it
clientSecret, a service's secret at its issuer as a program's record of it names it
client_secret, the same as the grant that spends it names it
secret: a member of that name holds one, whatever it is the secret of
password: a member of that name holds one, whatever it opens
authorization, the header a credential is sent under, among the headers of a request a result repeats
Authorization, the same header in its other spelling
x-api-key, the header one inference provider takes its key under
x-goog-api-key, the header another takes its key under

a name that only contains one of the names is another name, and is shown: the member that names the environment variable a credential is read from, an issuer's endpoint, who a request is authenticated as, and where authorization is had
